newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds close higher amid uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds close higher amid uncertainty.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed slightly higher on Sunday while traders waited to see if the attorney general would indict Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in wake of a corruption scandal. Indices:
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.1 pct to 105.26
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.12 to 104.28

"Two things affected trade today. The impending decision by the attorney general and the publication of the interest rates later this month along with the holiday of Passover which is starting tomorrow," said Ron Weisberg of IBI Investment House.
"Not much will happen during the holiday season and until the interest rates are published," he said.

The future of the entire government is uncertain in the wake of a corruption scandal surrounding Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Israel's attorney general is expected to announce later on Sunday whether to charge Netanyahu.
The Bank of Israel will announce on Thursday its monetary programme for May. Its base rate has remained at an annualised 13.9 percnet since the end of February.
The market was drifting upwards and was stable awaiting the decisions, Weisberg said.
Prices of CPI-linked bonds closed slightly higher with yields averaging 4.3 percent.

"There is uncertainty in the market but not as much as expected. When there is big uncertainty the demand for CPI-linked bonds and dollar-linked bonds goes up a lot, but today trading was quiet," said Dany Shamir at Israel Discount Bank.
Trading in dollar linked bonds was stable while there was a rise in demand for unlinked bonds and Makams, traders said.
On Monday and Tuesday the stock exchange will remain closed for the Jewish holiday of Passover.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
